inputs.root_cause: SAFETENSORS-LAZY-001's two obligations ('Provide header-only validation, read-only path mapping, tensor-relative region views, configurable size limits, and machine-readable access-strategy disclosure' / 'Large sparse-file tests prove header bytes copied, mapping mode, bounded Python allocations, and borrowed-view lifetime behavior') were both cited against the same five generic selectors (mostly header-layout parsing tests, not lazy/region-access tests) with no negative selectors, left at partial with the boilerplate missing_behavior placeholder -- despite three dedicated test files (test_lazy_io.py, test_obligation_tensor_regions.py, test_reference_header_layout_lazy_slice.py) already existing with real, on-point coverage of every single clause in both obligations' required_tests text.

execution_steps: 1. Continued the safetensors sweep after SAFETENSORS-LIFECYCLE-001. Read codec/reader/reader.py's load()/loads()/safe_open() in full: load(path) uses a genuine read-only mmap.mmap(..., access=mmap.ACCESS_READ) for zero-copy tensor-relative region access (PayloadAccessMode.MEMORY_MAPPED); loads(bytes) borrows the caller's buffer (BORROWED_BUFFER); load(non-seekable stream) discloses BUFFERED_STREAM honestly rather than claiming the same zero-copy guarantee it cannot provide. Every path returns a PayloadAccess record (model/document.py) -- the exact 'machine-readable access-strategy disclosure' this obligation names.

2. Searched for existing lazy/region/mmap-related tests and found three dedicated files already covering essentially every required_tests clause: test_lazy_io.py (header-only-and-mapped-region-bounded, stream-buffering-disclosure), test_obligation_tensor_regions.py (read-only mapped views without copy, region bounds fail closed), and test_reference_header_layout_lazy_slice.py (header-only validation not reading payload, path-backed readonly mapping and tensor-relative views, configurable header-limit enforcement, stream-backed buffered-not-zero-copy disclosure, a tracemalloc-measured 64MB-sparse-tensor bounded-allocation test, and a borrowed-view double-release-after-close safety test).
3. Ran all 16 candidate selectors directly before citing any of them (including the tensor_relative_region_bounds_fail_closed parametrization, 6 cases): all passed.

4. Read the sparse-file test body carefully before writing implemented_behavior to avoid overclaiming: it proves peak Python allocation (tracemalloc) stays under 4MB while reading a 16-byte tail region of a declared 64MB tensor -- i.e. payload is never materialized into Python memory regardless of declared size. It does NOT specifically isolate 'only header bytes are copied' as a measured claim, so the citation text was phrased to match exactly what tracemalloc actually measures, not a broader unverified claim.

5. Corrected both obligations' source_symbols (added SafeTensorsDocument.tensor_region, PayloadAccess, PayloadAccessMode, SafeTensorsDocument.close -- none of which were previously cited despite being directly exercised), positive/negative selectors (each obligation cites its own precise, non-identical subset matching its specific emphasis -- the first on the full access-strategy-disclosure surface, the second on the sparse-file/view-lifetime specifics), and promoted both to implemented. Zero source or test changes -- pure evidence correction.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/safetensors/ -q -- unchanged from before this slice (0 source or test changes)

evidence.oracle: none -- this is format_factory's own self-consistent test evidence (including tracemalloc-measured memory bounds, which is a genuine empirical measurement but not a comparison against an independent reference implementation). Labeled SELF-CONSISTENT per the FF6 execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not VERIFIED.
evidence.why_no_new_production_source: load()/safe_open()'s mmap-based zero-copy region access, PayloadAccess disclosure, and view-release lifecycle were already complete, correct, and covered by dedicated tests -- this slice's job was citing that proof accurately, not building anything new.
